title: Automated batching & caching optimizer with safe rollout controller
creator: Alex Chen
description:
Goal: Build an automated recommendation and apply pipeline that adjusts batching and prefix/KV cache parameters to reduce per-token cost while preserving latency and throughput SLOs. The system must be able to propose parameter sets, apply them progressively (canary -> ramp -> full), detect anomalies (regressions in p50/p95/p99 latency, queueing, dropped requests), and rollback safely with minimal disruption.

Scope: optimizer engine for live traffic that suggests and (optionally) applies changes to: target batch size distributions, max concurrent batches, prefix/KV cache TTLs and eviction policies, and model variant routing weights (quantized vs full). Integrations: Redwood Console (observability hooks and rollout UI), Runtime control plane (apply config + safe rollback API), Optimize recommendations console, and alerting (PagerDuty/SLO-driven alerts).

Non-goals: replacing manual SLO tuning; offline-only tuning; model training changes. This work focuses on inference-time config and routing changes only.
acceptance_criteria: Optimizer can generate candidate batch/cache profiles for a given production route with estimated cost delta and estimated latency impact (dashboard-visible)
Config apply supports staged rollout: canary (0.5-1%), ramp (10/50%), and full, with automatic pause on SLO violation and automatic rollback API
Anomaly detector flags increases in p95 or p99 latency beyond configurable thresholds within 2 minutes and triggers rollback when configured SLO guardrail is breached
SLO-aware router can divert a configurable fraction of traffic to fallback variants when latency degradation is detected
All changes are audited (who/what/when) and appear in Console with token-level cost delta and time-series comparisons
Integration tests that simulate traffic profile shifts validate safe rollback behavior and no request loss during canary transitions
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Simulate: run optimizer on historical traces and produce candidate sets (no apply)
Phase 1 - Readonly Canary: apply candidate to a shadowed canary environment and compare metrics for 24h
Phase 2 - Live Canary: 0.5% traffic, 30m observation window, auto-pause on anomaly
Phase 3 - Progressive Ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 30m hold and health-check gating
Phase 4 - Full Apply: mark candidate as default if all gates pass and persist audit
Emergency Rollback: immediate revert to previous config with warmup conservative settings + notify on-call
measurements: Primary metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), requests_per_second (RPS), successful_batches_per_second, average_batch_size, cache_prefix_hit_rate, cost_per_token (USD)
Derived safety signals: increase in request queue length, increase in backend GPU utilization > 10% over baseline, increase in error rate > 0.1% absolute
Anomaly thresholds default: p95 +15% over baseline OR p99 +10% over baseline => warning; p95 +30% OR p99 +20% => automatic rollback
mitigation_steps: Auto-pause rollout and revert to previous committed config
Fallback routing: shift traffic to compatible model variant (quantized->full or higher-concurrency variant)
Throttle ingress at API gateway for impacted route to preserve overall cluster health
If rollback fails or metric abnormal persists, trigger manual incident and run 'Config Stabilize' procedure from playbook
updates: 2025-02-18: Ticket created. Initial scoping and owners assigned. Decided to include model-variant routing as a mitigation vector.
2025-02-21: Prototype anomaly detector using ETS-based change detection completed against historical 7-day traces. False positive rate ~3% on weekdays.
2025-02-26: Runtime control-plane API PR opened (see runtime PR #4821). Canary gating hooks defined: metrics snapshot + health checks.
2025-03-01: Integration test harness added to CI to simulate traffic surges and verify automatic rollback; two flaky tests under investigation.
2025-03-03: Ops reviewed playbook; agreed on conservative default thresholds. Next: finalize UI for recommendation review in Console and add audit events for every apply/rollback
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive batching reduces cost but increases head-of-line latency for short requests. We bias optimizer towards SLO preservation by default (cost savings capped by allowed latency delta).
Decision: default behavior will be 'recommend-only' for new routes; auto-apply permitted only after explicit enable flag per customer/team
KV cache TTL tuning: prefer increasing TTL for stable prefixes and per-route configurable eviction policies. Avoid extending TTL for routes with highly dynamic user prompts due to stale cache risk.
Open question: how to quantify cross-route cache contamination when shared pool is used—tracking required in next spike of work
Dependency note: rely on ENG-12045's limiter APIs for enforcement of in-flight token/concurrency caps during rollout
